title: Best Smoke Alarms UK
short: Smoke alarms compared by response time, alarm volume and smart features, from simple 9V battery alarms to interlinked smart systems with CO detection.
intro: A working smoke alarm makes you roughly 12 times less likely to die in a house fire, according to the National Fire Chiefs Council, and response speed and loudness matter more than smart features. This guide compares alarms tested by Expert Reviews using an aerosol tester and a sound meter to measure real response times and volume.

products.name: Nest Protect (2nd Generation)
products.badge: Best smart smoke and CO alarm
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most polished smart alarm with phone alerts
products.key_spec: Split-spectrum optical sensor, 10-year CO sensor, 98.7dBA alarm
products.summary: Still the smart alarm to beat, according to Expert Reviews, with an advanced sensor spotting both smouldering and fast-flaring fires, plus temperature, humidity, light and motion sensors. It took 7.12 seconds to register a test spray, gives phone alerts and a voice warning before full alarm, and even lights up to guide your way in the dark.
pros: Easy to use with clear alerts
cons: Limited integration with other Nest/Google audio products

products.name: Link+ Pro (3-Alarm Bundle with Base Station)
products.best_for: Buyers who want whole-home interlinked coverage without Nest Protect pricing
products.key_spec: 3 alarms + wireless Base Station, 99.1dBA siren, app control
products.summary: Roughly £80 covers three alarms plus a base station, enough for the average UK home, which Expert Reviews had running within 15 minutes. Any alarm going off triggers all of them with voice alerts, app notifications and email, though the app is less polished than Nest's and response time is a touch slower at 7.51 seconds.
pros: Loud alerts across the whole home
Easy to use with app-based test/hush
cons: App less polished and flexible than Nest Protect
products.search: X-Sense Link Plus Pro smoke alarm

products.name: DY29 Smoke Alarm with Hush
products.best_for: Buyers who just want a fast, reliable, no-frills alarm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this the fastest alarm on test, sounding in just 2.44 seconds after the test spray, with no compromise on volume at a piercing 97.6dBA. It's compact, easy to fit, and a single button both hushes and tests the alarm, though the 9V battery needs replacing roughly every year.
cons: Only basic features, no smart connectivity

products.name: SD-S01E
products.best_for: Buyers already invested in an Aqara or Zigbee smart home setup
products.summary: Uses the Zigbee protocol rather than WiFi for a more stable, energy-efficient connection, though it requires Aqara's own Hub M2 or M3 rather than third-party Zigbee hubs. Expert Reviews found it reasonably sensitive at 7.25 seconds and loud at 93.7dBA, but had trouble getting it working reliably with Google Home despite Matter compliance.
pros: Good option for existing Aqara/Zigbee setups
cons: Requires a separate, costly Aqara hub
Google Home integration proved unreliable in testing

products.name: SC07-WX
products.badge: Best combined smoke and CO alarm
products.best_for: Rooms with a fuel-burning appliance needing both smoke and CO protection
products.key_spec: Combined smoke and CO detection, WiFi, LCD screen, 98.8dBA
products.summary: A chunkier unit that packs in both a smoke detector and a chemical CO detector with a basic LCD readout. Expert Reviews found it worked well as both, registering smoke within 6.6 seconds and CO within 4 seconds, with WiFi giving the same app alerts as the Link+ Pro, though it's comparatively bulky.
pros: Combines smoke and CO detection in one unit
Fast response for both smoke and CO
cons: Comparatively bulky, needs plenty of ceiling space
products.search: X-Sense SC07-WX smoke and CO alarm

products.name: CV2106
products.best_for: Blocks of flats or larger homes where you might not hear a distant siren
products.key_spec: 78mm diameter, sealed 10-year lithium battery, RF interlinking
products.summary: Complies with UK regulations for rented properties, with a sealed battery lasting the full 10-year lifespan and the ability to link multiple units so one alarm echoes through all. Expert Reviews found it responded in 5.94 seconds, a little slower than the Kidde DY29, but just as loud at 96.1dBA, with a flashing LED visual alert too.
cons: Slightly slower response than the simplest alarms

products.name: K2007
products.best_for: Boats, caravans and other cramped spaces
products.summary: At just 4cm across, this is a genuinely tiny alarm that Expert Reviews still found highly effective, registering the test spray in under seven seconds and putting out an ear-splitting 101.4dBA when triggered. The sealed lithium battery lasts the unit's full ten-year lifespan, with the top doubling as both test and hush button.
pros: Very loud despite the small size
cons: Quite expensive for a basic alarm

guide.q: How many smoke alarms do I need, and where?
guide.a: The National Fire Chiefs Council recommends at least one smoke alarm on each level of your home, plus a heat alarm in the kitchen since heat alarms are less prone to false triggers from cooking. Test all alarms regularly, and replace any older alarms, since sensors deteriorate over time regardless of how the alarm is powered.

guide.q: Do my smoke alarms need to be interlinked by law?
guide.a: Interlinked alarms, where one going off triggers all of them, are a legal requirement in all homes in Scotland and in private rented homes in Wales. Even where not legally required, the NFCC recommends them as a genuinely useful option, since you're far more likely to hear an alarm from another room or floor.

A 9V battery alarm, like the Kidde DY29 here, is cheap but needs annual battery replacement. Long-life lithium battery alarms, increasingly common and required for Scotland's 10-year rule, need no replacement for the alarm's full working life. Both are valid as long as you actually replace batteries or the whole unit when due.

guide.q: Do I need a smart, app-connected smoke alarm?
guide.a: A smart alarm, like the Nest Protect or X-Sense options here, sends phone alerts even when you're not home, which is genuinely valuable for detecting a fire while out or asleep in a large house. A simple standalone alarm, like the Kidde DY29, still protects you effectively at home for a fraction of the price if smart features aren't a priority.
